behind_the_meter.name: Data Center Aruba IT1
behind_the_meter.status: None at this site. Aruba owns eleven hydroelectric plants across Piedmont, Lombardy, Veneto and Friuli Venezia Giulia totalling about 11.6 MW and producing more than 60 GWh a year, on the Brembo, Lambro, Astico, Fella and Stura di Lanzo, and photovoltaic panels covering the usable sunlit surfaces of the Bergamo campus. One of the Brembo plants adjoins the Ponte San Pietro campus. None of this capacity is at Arezzo, and Aruba describes the output as flowing into the national electricity system and helping balance group demand rather than feeding a data centre directly. Electricity at Arezzo IT1 is bought from the grid with Guarantee of Origin renewable certificates.

behind_the_meter.name: xAI Macrohardrr
behind_the_meter.type: Natural gas turbines. 41 permanent units are permitted, replacing temporary mobile turbines that are being phased out.
behind_the_meter.status: Under construction as of xAI's July 30, 2026 statement. Temporary mobile turbines were operating in the interim, with removal to begin August 2026 and finish by July 2027.

name: Power and grid
answer: These measures show how a data center gets its electricity: its place in the interconnection queue, what capacity costs on the market, power generated on site and long-term power contracts. Power is now the main limit on where and how fast AI data centers can be built.

metrics.line: The share of an interconnection queue that has cleared study and holds final approval to draw power, as opposed to sitting as a request. Queue totals count paper; approval to energize counts electricity.
metrics.label: Approval to energize versus queued load

metrics.line: In grid regions with a capacity market, the auction-cleared price paid per megawatt-day for generators to guarantee availability years ahead.
metrics.label: Capacity market clearing price

metrics.line: Dedicated on-site power, gas turbines, microgrids, storage, or eventually reactors, wired directly to the facility rather than drawn through a public grid connection.
metrics.label: Behind-the-meter generation

metrics.line: A generator's or large load's place in the regional grid operator's study process, with waits commonly measured in years.
metrics.label: Interconnection queue position and wait

metrics.line: Long-term contracts by which operators secure generation, nuclear, solar, wind, or gas, for current and future facilities.
metrics.label: Power purchase agreements
